citeAs: Goyal, Naman, Cynthia Gao, Vishrav Chaudhary, Peng-Jen Chen, Guillaume Wenzek, Da Ju, Sanjana Krishnan, Marc’Aurelio Ranzato, Francisco Guzmán, Angela Fan (2021). The FLORES-101 Evaluation Benchmark for Low-Resource and Multilingual Machine Translation. arXiv.
creator: Naman Goyal, Cynthia Gao, Vishrav Chaudhary, Peng-Jen Chen, Guillaume Wenzek, Da Ju, Sanjana Krishnan, Marc’Aurelio Ranzato, Francisco Guzmán, Angela Fan (Facebook AI Research, LORIA)
description: FLORES-101 is a multilingual machine translation evaluation benchmark consisting of 3001 sentences extracted from English Wikipedia and professionally translated into 101 languages. The sentences are multilingually aligned and include metadata to support many-to-many translation evaluation, as well as document-level and multimodal evaluation.
name: FLORES-101
rai:annotationsPerItem: Each sentence received at least one professional translation and subsequent quality-assurance evaluation; translations could go through additional rounds of re-translation and re-evaluation if quality was insufficient.
rai:annotatorDemographics: For sentence selection, the paper states that 10 annotators in the authors' lab performed selection: 6 male and 4 female; with roles including researchers (scientists and engineers) and program/project managers; originally from East Asia, South Asia, Southern Europe, Latin America, and North America.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Translation quality was assessed with a Translation Quality Score on a 0 to 100 scale based on identified errors in grammar, punctuation, spelling, capitalization, addition or omission, mistranslation, unnatural translation, untranslated text, and register, with minor, major, and critical severities. The acceptable translation quality score was set to 90%, and all 101 released languages met this threshold.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Sentences were translated by professional translators through language service providers, then edited within the provider, checked automatically, and evaluated by an independent quality-assurance provider. If automatic checks failed or human quality scores were below threshold, translations were sent back for re-translation.
rai:dataBiases: The paper explicitly notes efforts to avoid bias from document structure by selecting one paragraph per document from the beginning, middle, or end and balancing these positions across the corpus. It also discusses the potential risk of translationese because all source sentences are in English and non-English source sentences are human translations, though the authors argue the benefits of many-to-many evaluation outweigh this risk.
rai:dataCollection: The source sentences were extracted from English Wikipedia-related Wikimedia sources. The dataset construction had three phases: sourcing sentences, pilot experiments to define translation and evaluation processes, and large-scale translation across more than 100 languages using language service providers with automatic and human quality checks.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data consisted of English sentences extracted from Wikimedia sources, specifically Wikinews, Wikijunior, and WikiVoyage articles, along with metadata such as Wikipedia URL, topic, and boolean flags for linked entities and images.
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: The paper reports an average of 26 days to translate one language, 35 days to re-translate, and 61 days total on average per language, with the shortest turnaround 31 days and longest 89 days.
rai:dataLimitations: The paper notes that sourcing all sentences from English means non-English source sentences are human translations, creating possible translationese effects. It also notes that some languages considered for inclusion were not released because they could not meet the quality bar after re-translation.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: After collection, the corpus was split into dev, devtest, and test sets. The sentence selection process balanced paragraph position within documents across beginning, middle, and end. Translations could undergo iterative re-translation based on automatic checks and human evaluation.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Sentence selection involved randomly selecting articles from each source and manually choosing 3 to 5 contiguous sentences while avoiding very short or malformed sentences. Automatic quality-control preprocessing for translations included language identification, copy detection against source text, length-difference checks, language-model fluency checks, and similarity checks against commercial translation engine outputs.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The authors state that publicly releasing a high-quality, high-coverage dataset is intended to foster progress in the machine translation community and beyond, especially for low-resource languages spoken by large populations who could benefit from improved translation quality.
rai:dataUseCases: Intended uses include evaluation of low-resource and multilingual machine translation, especially many-to-many multilingual translation systems. The dataset is also intended to support document-level translation, multimodal translation, text classification, sentence and document classification, language identification, multilingual domain adaptation, and related evaluations.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Automatic checks used language identification, language-model fluency checks, and sentence-level SentencePiece BLEU similarity heuristics against outputs of public or commercial translation engines to detect copied translations.

null_reasons.inLanguage: the paper lists 101 languages mostly with ISO 639-3 codes and names, but the field requires ISO 639-1 codes and many included languages do not have ISO 639-1 codes, so a compliant value cannot be derived from the paper alone
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: no crowdsourcing or annotation platform is named; only language service providers are described
null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: the paper does not discuss missing data or missing observations in the dataset
null_reasons.rai:dataImputationProtocol: no imputation or fill-in strategy for missing values is described
null_reasons.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: no explicit dataset maintenance, versioning, or update plan is described
